[42890 4G/5G Mobile Technologies | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject equips you with a comprehensive understanding of 4G and 5G wireless communication systems, with a strong emphasis on wireless propagation, antenna design and analysis. You'll gain foundational knowledge of the structure, functions, and behaviour of 4G/5G networks and learn to use engineering tools to design antennas and assess wireless propagation performance. You will learn about system architecture, radio systems, wave propagation, MIMO beamforming, antennas and fundamental parameters. The subject is vendor-neutral and adheres to industry standards, preparing you for a career in telecommunications engineering.

[42890 4G/5G Mobile Technologies | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject delivery of lectures, tutorials, and quizzes. It is the responsibility of the student to read UTS Canvas regularly, watch the lecture videos, study the subject resources, and answer the review questions. The students gain first exposure to new material outside of class, usually via subject readings and lecture videos on Canvas, and then class time is used for tutorials to learn hands-on electromagnetic simulation skills, answer questions and for assimilating that knowledge through strategies such as quizzes, problem-solving, presentations, discussion or debates. The modelling and practices are performed by students outside class times in groups to encourage collaborative learning. 

The subject is designed so that students engage with the subject material with weekly quizzes and final exam. This organisation results in continuous self-assessment throughout the session to ensure that student learning is appropriate and ‘on-track’. Past experience has shown that students who miss key learning activities have a high chance of failure. We expect that students play an active part in their learning in the subject and adhere to the principles of good academic practice. This means that students should come to all of the class sessions well prepared. Go through the lecture videos and subject resources BEFORE coming to class. Take an active part in the class and engage with the learning activities – students should not simply be passive observers! The exams and quizzes assume that students have completed the readings and lecture videos along with the lecture notes. 

To support students in navigating an AI-enhanced engineering environment, the 4G/5G Mobile Technologies subject will incorporate guided use of generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot. These tools are not presented as shortcuts, but as intelligent collaborators that assist in the design and analysis of wireless systems. Students will be encouraged to use AI to brainstorm network design ideas, interpret electromagnetic simulation results, clarify technical standards, draft and refine design reports and diagrams, and receive formative feedback on their understanding of wireless communication concepts. With in-class guidance, students will learn to critically evaluate AI-generated content in the context of telecommunications engineering, understanding both its capabilities and its limitations. All AI use will be aligned with academic integrity standards, helping students build digital literacy alongside authentic and discipline-specific skills. 

The teaching strategy consists of weekly classes made up of a one-hour lecture followed by a tutorial session. Lecture recording will be made available in Canvas before the class for students to watch and prepare for the week's content. Design tasks are then undertaken to apply concepts.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[42890 4G/5G Mobile Technologies | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Explain the principles of 4G and 5G physical layer technologies, including radio system, wave propagation, and antenna structures, in the context of wireless system performance. (D.1)
SLO2: Analyse and model key physical components of mobile networks using electromagnetic simulation tools to evaluate performance under realistic conditions. (D.1)
SLO3: Design and validate innovative antenna solutions for 4G and 5G systems through simulation, optimisation, and performance benchmarking. (C.1)
SLO4: Collaborate in teams to deliver a professional wireless design project in a realistic hands-on antenna engineering context, demonstrating technical communication skills. (E.1)
